stories.name: GE Aerospace stock outlook
stories.blurb: A series of headlines weighing whether GE Aerospace's strong earnings and rally make its stock a buy, a sell, or overvalued versus rivals like Boeing, Lockheed Martin, and SpaceX.

stories.name: Archer-Boeing Deal
stories.blurb: Archer Aviation is acquiring Boeing subsidiaries Wisk Aero, Insitu, and SkyGrid, a deal that boosts Archer's growth prospects and stock price in the eVTOL/air taxi market.

stories.name: Boeing Q3 cash flow troubles
stories.blurb: Boeing's third-quarter results and weak cash flow outlook have driven analyst downgrades and a sharp stock decline.

stories.name: Boeing F/A-XX Contract Win
stories.blurb: Boeing won a roughly $20 billion U.S. Navy contract to build the next-generation F/A-XX carrier fighter, sending its stock higher.

stories.name: Boeing 737 Max 10 certification
stories.blurb: Boeing's long-delayed 737 Max 10 is working through FAA certification, hampered by software issues and production constraints, as the company pushes toward approval and ramps up output.

stories.name: Defense Stocks Surge
stories.blurb: Rising government defense spending, missile stockpile initiatives, and strong earnings are driving a broad rally in defense and aerospace stocks like Lockheed Martin, RTX, and Rocket Lab.

stories.name: Boeing market reports
stories.blurb: A series of market research reports forecasting growth across commercial aircraft, cabin, and defense segments, with Boeing named among the leading manufacturers driving demand through 2030.

past.name: Aerospace Q3 earnings
past.blurb: Third-quarter earnings results and investor reaction across major aerospace companies, including Boeing, GE Aerospace, Hexcel, Honeywell, RTX, and United Airlines.

past.name: Boeing 737 Max certification
past.blurb: Boeing is working through regulatory certification and production delays for its 737 Max variants while trying to stabilize output.

past.name: Boeing Regulatory & Orders Update
past.blurb: Boeing navigates FAA regulatory approvals, safety inspections, and emissions exemptions while securing new aircraft orders and deliveries across its commercial jet lineup.

11.text: A market report projects the global narrowbody aircraft market at $126.9 billion, with Airbus, Boeing, and GE Aerospace positioned to benefit from fuel-efficient fleet demand. Other articles cover GE Aerospace's stock, aerospace/defense ETFs, and TransDigm's Q4 results, bearing on Boeing only indirectly.

6.text: Archer's Q3 revenue beat at $5.1M but losses exceeded expectations, sending shares down despite $1.4B cash. Its pending acquisition of three Boeing businesses would add over $200M in annual revenue, with LA air taxi launch and 2027 passenger service targets progressing.

5.text: Boeing posted positive free cash flow, won Avolon’s record 140-jet 737-10 order, and two directors bought shares, but October deliveries fell and it will cut about 5% of its commercial workforce.

10.text: Northrop Grumman will not protest the Navy's F/A-XX award to Boeing, clearing Boeing's path on the next-generation carrier-based fighter. Other articles cover BAE Systems' LRASM sensor deliveries and KC-135 repairs, plus defense earnings, barely involving Boeing.

8.text: Boeing will cut 5% of its commercial airplane workers because 737 Max production increases are taking longer than expected. The planes are built outside Seattle.

7.text: Nvidia and Cisco led Dow declines on Nov 5, with Boeing among the index's biggest losers that session. On Nov 6 the Dow fell after a strong October jobs report while Nvidia rebounded.

13.text: ResearchAndMarkets.com released market reports forecasting growth to 2030 across commercial aircraft, narrowbody, single-aisle, cabin interiors, helicopter, and reconnaissance segments. Boeing is named among leading manufacturers in each, but the articles contain no Boeing-specific news or developments.
